findings.message: If a `max_iterations` cycle entry in the state file is missing `iterations_used` or `max_iterations` fields, `_convergence_json` carries JSON `null` for those values and the rendered convergence line shows `(null/null iterations)` instead of real counts, giving the operator no usable information.

The `_extra` block (convergence warning and failing-gate lines) is appended after `"Generated by zBuild automation."`, so the safety-critical operator notice appears below the footer rather than in a prominent position; acceptance criteria check for string presence, not position, so tests pass, but the warning is easy to overlook.

When `state.status` is `"failed"` (SPEC-1) but no cycle has `status == "max_iterations"` (SPEC-2 does not apply), `_convergence_json` remains `[]` and `_pr_open_render_convergence_section` emits nothing; SPEC-3 says the body must include a convergence section when SPEC-1 applies, so a failed-but-converged run produces a draft PR with no convergence text, leaving the operator with only the gate section (if present) as context.

`_max_iter_count` is computed with a dedicated `jq` process then `_convergence_json` is computed with a second `jq` process using the identical `.cycle_iterations … select(.value.status == "max_iterations")` filter; `_max_iter_count > 0` is fully implied by `_convergence_json != "[]"`, so the first spawn and the numeric check are dead weight.

Three separate `jq` subshells are forked on `state_file` (status, count, convergence JSON) where a single `jq` call producing a composite object would suffice; the overhead is bounded to one PR-open per run but the pattern sets a precedent for accumulation.

`_pr_open_render_gate_section` forks three `jq` subshells on the same `gate_path` (verdict, failed list, reason) where a single `jq` call projecting all three fields at once would eliminate two process-spawn round-trips.

When an existing open PR is found, the code calls `gh pr edit` with only `--title` and `--body`, never consulting `_gh_args`; the `--draft` flag forced by the new SPEC-1/SPEC-2 logic is silently dropped, so a non-draft PR opened by a prior passing run remains non-draft after a failed or unconverged re-run.

Gate-aggregator `failed_gates` and `reason` strings are interpolated into the PR body via bare `printf` without the `esc` sanitiser (strips ANSI, control chars, escapes `\`,`[`,`]`,`<`,`>`) that every other value rendered in this file passes through.

`cycle_id`, `iterations_used`, and `max_iterations` extracted from the state file are interpolated into the PR body via `jq -r` string interpolation without the `esc` sanitiser used for all advisory findings rendered elsewhere in this file.

The `reason` and `failed_gates` fields extracted from gate_aggregator_result are reflected verbatim into the PR body without any sanitization; if the gate-aggregator artifact were compromised, arbitrary markdown or HTML could be injected into the published PR.

The `cycle_id` field from pipeline-state.json is interpolated directly into PR-body markdown via jq's `\(.cycle_id)` without sanitization; a malicious or malformed state file could inject arbitrary markdown into the PR.

The emit_event at plugin.result emission does not include draft status or the reason draft was forced (failed_status or max_iterations), so operators cannot identify forced-draft events in structured logs without inspecting pr-result.json manually.

The existing-PR update path (gh pr edit) does not pass --draft or call gh pr convert-to-draft, so a failed re-run that finds an existing non-draft PR updates the body with the convergence warning but leaves the PR as non-draft, violating the issue's requirement that a failed run never presents its output as ready to merge.

The convergence and gate warning blocks (_extra) are appended after 'Generated by zBuild automation.' at the end of the PR body, reducing operator visibility of the non-convergence alert compared to the issue's example placement.
